title: The Wrong Intermezzo
premise: A lyrical ABACBA serenade is repeatedly interrupted by a different, dry electronic personality; a structural paraphrase of Bartók’s Interrupted Intermezzo, not a melodic transcription.

title: Crossing on the Stairs
premise: Opposing continuous acceleration/deceleration canons, inspired by the crossing speeds of Nancarrow’s Study 21; shaped sentences and new instrumental speakers preserve a perceptible process.

title: Pocket Gongs, Plugged In
premise: Nested gong-like cycles, split wind melodies, and unequal dance groups meet DI guitars and resonant leads; structural borrowings, not a claim to perform any one tradition authentically.

title: The Counting Choir
premise: An original synthetic speaking voice counts Fibonacci numbers and comments on the tuning; a fixed-pitch formant vocoder turns its syllables into a strange dry choir.

title: One Room, Twenty Doors
premise: Twenty short doors: a promenade-like returning figure connects different borrowed formal devices, places and composerly habits; only public-domain tunes are actually quoted.

title: Brother Jacques at the Wrong Funeral
premise: Frère Jacques, Dies irae and a tiny familiar cadential joke are re-pitched into the actual fields, passed between acoustic instruments and analog/FM leads, then contradicted.

title: Butterfly Relays
premise: The only tremolo piece: soft continuous tremolo, deep square audio gates, and many independently pulsing sustained layers. No other piece uses periodic amplitude gates.

title: Five People, One Cable
premise: A close, conversational five-player ensemble with tiny shared timing inflections, DI guitar, Rhodes and a modular voice; selected instrument bodies exchange their spectral color without room reverb.

title: Take Your Cables Home
premise: A reverse accumulation: players stop, exchange their last phrases, and leave. The ending borrows the departure mechanism of Haydn’s Farewell, without a volume fade.

title: Jo, Ha, Trapdoor
premise: Free introductions, drawn-out melody, asymmetric pulse and a fast exit: an original jo–ha–kyū-inspired trajectory, with early previews, counterpoint, brief detours, and no borrowed gagaku melody.
